proposals.text:
Thanks — I pulled your recent card transactions. I can check these on your behalf, but before I open any formal investigation I want to confirm which transactions you want me to look into.

What I found (quick scan)
- Most transactions show rewards recorded as "points" (our system stores rewards as points; 1 point = $0.01 when redeemed).
- Many transactions show rewards equal to roughly the dollar amount (e.g., $89.99 → 89 points), which is consistent with a 1 point per $1 baseline.
- There are a number of transactions where the recorded points are noticeably higher than the dollar amount — those are the ones we should review for miscategorization, wrong bonus application, or improper rate application.

I pulled the full list of your last ~2 months of posted transactions. Here are the ones that stand out (transactions where rewards posted are much higher than the numeric dollar amount):

1) Slack Technologies — 10/15/2025 — $44.67 — rewards: 178 points  
2) DTE Energy (Crypto-Cash Back card) — 10/17/2025 — $97.41 — rewards: 194 points  
3) Google Ads (Business Platinum) — 10/18/2025 — $187.56 — rewards: 1875 points  
4) Southwest Airlines — 10/19/2025 — $323.89 — rewards: 1295 points  
5) JetBlue Airways — 10/21/2025 — $278.94 — rewards: 1115 points  
6) GitHub Enterprise — 10/27/2025 — $255.68 — rewards: 1022 points  
7) Microsoft 365 — 11/03/2025 — $79.99 — rewards: 319 points  
8) AWS (Business Platinum) — 10/30/2025 — $1,247.83 — rewards: 4,991 points  
9) United Airlines (Business Platinum) — 11/02/2025 — $347.62 — rewards: 521 points (note: this one posts lower than other travel items — included because it differs from some travel multipliers)  
10) Home Depot — 10/27/2025 — $291.43 — rewards: 582 points (about 2x)

Why I flagged these
- They differ from the simpler pattern seen on many purchases (points roughly equal to the dollar amount). Differences can happen for legitimate reasons: card-specific bonus categories (e.g., travel, media, software, green merchants), promotional bonuses, or merchant-category classification that results in a higher rate. They can also be caused by miscategorization or system errors.

How I can help next (choose one)
A) I can investigate up to 10 of these transactions for you now. I’ll:
   - Verify the merchant category and applicable reward rate for the transaction date,
   - Confirm whether the posted rewards match the correct rate,
   - If we find an error, start the correction process (I’ll open an internal investigation and, if required by our process, apply corrections or escalate to the rewards team).  
   Please tell me which of the above (or any other transactions from your list) you want me to investigate. If you want me to investigate all 10 listed, say “Investigate all 10.”

B) If you prefer, I can instead walk you through what each flagged transaction appears to show and suggest which ones most likely need investigation (no formal case opened yet).

Notes and limits
- If we open formal corrections, some adjustments may require internal steps and an audit trail. If a dispute requires provisional credit, eligibility rules apply (e.g., account age, dispute reason, minimum amount). I can advise on provisional credit if it becomes relevant.
- I will not change anything without your consent to investigate/open a case.

Which option would you like, and which specific transactions should I investigate (or should I investigate all 10)?
